sink.buffer: RTP timestamp-based, 4096 samples (~93ms) negotiated in RECORD response. Receiver clamps far-future NTP scheduling — sender-side delay in AudioBroadcaster is the only way to shift playback.
quirks: Silently drops ALAC frames with escape=1 (verbatim/raw PCM). Music.app never emits these. Send only compressed ALAC via AVAudioConverter with kAudioFormatAppleLossless output.

Sync packets MUST originate from the source port advertised in SETUP's Transport header. Receiver kernel-rejects packets from any other source port (ICMP port unreachable). Use BSD socket bound to the advertised local control port.

Receiver advertises Audio-Latency: 4096 (= 93ms at 44.1kHz) and CLAMPS far-future NTP scheduling to that buffer depth. Setting manualOffsetSeconds=5.0 produces zero audible delay — receiver plays packets on arrival. Shift audio at the sender instead.

Controller-identifier headers (Client-Instance, DACP-ID) must be PER-RTSP-client-instance, not static-per-process. Sharing across concurrent sessions confuses firmware (treats new connection as stale prior session, refuses cold start).

notes: First B&W speaker validated end-to-end in SuperAudio. Reference profile for the AirPlay 1 receiver pattern. M3a gate-clearing device. Same wire format as the AirPort Express that B&W's firmware was derived from.
